reader_summary.headline: Hello everyone and welcome to Investing by the Books, a podcast by Radai.
reader_summary.overview: Hello everyone and welcome to Investing by the Books, a podcast by Radai. I'm your host, Edipamian, and for this episode we're thrilled to have Chris Mayer back on the show. Chris is a thoughtful US-based investor, running the fund Woodlockhouse Family Capital.

key_points.text: He is also the author of multiple books on investing and semantics.
key_points.evidence_quote: He is also the author of multiple books on investing and semantics.

key_points.text: And in episode 13, almost five years ago, we discussed his classic title, Hundred Baggers, about stocks that return 100 times your money.
key_points.evidence_quote: And in episode 13, almost five years ago, we discussed his classic title, Hundred Baggers, about stocks that return 100 times your money, and in many cases much more than that.

key_points.text: I'm a big fan of Chris's style as an investor and also how he writes.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm a big fan of Chris's style as an investor and also how he writes.

key_points.text: And the other year I did a Swedish translation of his book, Hundred Baggers, and in connection with that translation, I asked him.
key_points.evidence_quote: And the other year I did a Swedish translation of his book, Hundred Baggers, and in connection with that translation, I asked him, do you have any plans of ever releasing another investing book?

thesis: The episode introduces Chris Mayer, author of the upcoming book 'The Investor's Odyssey,' which is described as a qualitative, experiential meditation on long-term investing and the journey of owning a company. The book contrasts with his previous work, 'Hundred Baggers,' by shifting focus from a study of stocks that increased 100 times to reflections on the distractions, challenges, and obstacles encountered over a decade-plus of ownership.
